identity.name: Moravian Serbia

land.text: Lazar Hrebeljanović's principality in the Morava valley, 'established in 1371' (Cliopatria's Serbian Empire shape of 1375)

predecessors.note: After the Battle of Maritsa Lazar took part of the Mrnjavčević lands; in 1373 most of Nikola Altomanović's (Moravian Serbia page).

land.text: the Despotate's last Cliopatria shape; infobox 'Reconquest by the Ottoman Empire: 20 June 1459'

successors.note: Smederevo and the Morava lands; Novo Brdo already fell on 1 June 1455.

land.text: 'most of the Despotate's holdings west of the Drina', conquered by King Stjepan Tomaš after Lazar Branković's death in January 1458

successors.note: Stephen Tomašević held Serbia from 21 March to 20 June 1459 and lost Bosnia in 1463.

capitals.name: Kruševac
capitals.note: Infobox: capitals Kruševac and Belgrade; 'In the beginning of 1405, Stefan made Belgrade the capital of Serbia, replacing Kruševac' (Stefan Lazarević page).

capitals.name: Belgrade
capitals.note: Belgrade, Mačva and Golubac came from Sigismund in late 1403 or early 1404; Belgrade returned to Hungary on Stefan's death in 1427 (Serbian Despotate page).

capitals.name: Smederevo
capitals.note: Đurađ built Smederevo 'in 1428–1430' on the Danube; the infobox lists Beograd, Smederevo and Bar without years.

rulers.name: Lazar Hrebeljanović
rulers.title: Prince
rulers.note: Killed at the Battle of Kosovo, 28 June 1389 (Serbian Despotate page).

rulers.name: Stefan Lazarević
rulers.title: Prince, Despot from 1402
rulers.note: Milica administered the state while he was a minor; despot title in August 1402; died 19 July 1427 (Stefan Lazarević page).

rulers.name: Đurađ Branković
rulers.title: Despot
rulers.note: Succeeded 19 July 1427; confirmed as despot by John VIII Palaiologos in 1429.

correction.text: not used by moravian-serbia; the Serbian Empire of Dušan (1346-1371)

keyframe_review.note: Not this state: Cliopatria's Serbian Empire row (1352..1458) is split; this shape is the Serbian Empire proper (to 1371) and is reviewed in serbian-empire. The Moravian Serbia page dates this state's start to 1371.

correction.text: not used by moravian-serbia; see moravian-serbia_1371 for 1371-1374

keyframe_review.note: Not this state: Cliopatria's Serbian Empire row (1352..1458) is split; this shape is the Serbian Empire proper (to 1371) and is reviewed in serbian-empire. For 1371-1374, where the Empire row still runs, use moravian-serbia_1371.

correction.text: the 1375 shape, extended back to 1371; only the years are corrected

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1371-1374: 'The independent principality in the region of Morava was established in 1371'. Cliopatria's Serbian Empire row still draws the whole empire shape (184,871 km2) in these years and starts Lazar's land only in 1375; the 1375 shape (46,495 km2) is extended back, a soft reading since the page names no places for the Mrnjavčević land Lazar took in 1371 or for most of Altomanović's land (1373).

correction.text: unchanged for 1375-1385; from 1386 without the Niš area (ledger loss)

keyframe_review.note: 46,495 km2, capital Kruševac, area not given on the page. The shape runs to 1394 but 'Murad I took Niš from Lazar' in 1386 (the page gives no 1375 date for Niš, which the Cliopatria shape includes); it is right as drawn for 1375-1385 and the ledger removes Niš in 1386. Lazar took Braničevo and Kučevo in 1379, 'reaching the state's full extent'.

50,813 km2 (+9% on the 1375 shape). After Nicopolis (25 September 1396) 'Vuk Branković's land was taken by the Ottomans' and 'Most of his area was transferred to the control of Stefan Lazarević'; Cliopatria starts the larger shape a year earlier than that page, the ledger carries the gain at 1397. Vassalage of the Ottomans from the summer of 1390 does not change the drawn area (suzerain's dossier).

47,450 km2 (-6.6% on 1395-1401). After Angora (28 July 1402) Stefan received the title despot in August 1402 and the state 'became known as the Serbian Despotate in 1402'. In 1409 'practically, Stefan ceded the southeastern part of his lands to Vuk' (south of the West Morava); the page dates no return and Cliopatria's 1415 shape is larger again, so no loss is drawn. Belgrade, Mačva and Golubac (1403/1404) and Srebrenica (1411) are in the ledger as gains the shape may not hold.

67,678 km2, +43% on the 1402 shape (bbox now to 41.78 N and 18.96 E, Montenegro). No page opened dates a Despotate acquisition in 1415; the step may be Branković land in Kosovo and Polimlje ('parts of Kosovo, Polimlje, Sjenica and Brskovo' were Branković land by early 1402) or the Zeta hinterland under Stefan's influence since 1405. Unverified for 1415-1421 (page budget); the Zeta lordship itself is vassal land until 1421.

73,646 km2 (+5,968 km2 on 1415-1421). Matches the inheritance of Zeta: 'in 1421, before his death and under the influence of his mother, he [Balša III] passed the rule of Zeta to his uncle, Despot Stefan Lazarević' (Cliopatria's Serbian Despots row, probably Zeta, is 6,993 km2 in 1415-1421 and ends in 1421). Stefan Lazarević died 19 July 1427.

73,099 km2. Belgrade went back to Hungary in 1427 (ledger); the Cliopatria step is -0.7%, small for a capital and the Belgrade district, so the shape may still hold Belgrade's cells (unverified). Đurađ confirmed as despot in 1429; Smederevo 1428-1430. The Ottoman capture of Smederevo on 18 August 1439 and the restoration by the Peace of Szeged on 15 August 1444 are not in the shape (ledger occupation).
72,981 km2. Novo Brdo 'fell on June 27, 1441, and again on June 1, 1455'; the restored Serbia of 1444 had 'borders as before 1437' (Peace of Szeged, 15 August 1444). Southern Zeta stayed with Venice.

correction.text: unchanged shape, valid to 20 June 1459; the 1455 Novo Brdo and 1458 west-of-the-Drina losses are ledger events

keyframe_review.note: 70,132 km2 (-3.9%), the shape for 1453-1458; the Despotate does not end in 1458 but on 20 June 1459 ('officially conquered by the Turks'), so the shape is extended by one year. Novo Brdo fell on 1 June 1455 and 'most of the Despotate's holdings west of the Drina' went to Stjepan Tomaš of Bosnia after Lazar Branković's death in January 1458 (ledger).

region.text: Lazar's lands on the Morava, as Cliopatria's 1375 shape

ledger.note: 1371: Prince Lazar's principality on the Morava. 'The independent principality in the region of Morava was established in 1371'; after Maritsa Lazar took part of the Mrnjavčević land and in 1373, with Tvrtko I, defeated Nikola Altomanović, most of whose land went to Lazar (the page names no places). Capitals Kruševac and Belgrade (infobox).

1379: Lazar takes Braničevo and Kučevo and the state reaches its full extent. The page says only that 'Lazar took Braničevo and Kučevo'; the previous holder is not named (Radič Branković Rastislalić was ousted in 1379).
1386: Murad I takes Niš. The page says 'Murad I took Niš from Lazar'.

1397: Vuk Branković's lands pass to Stefan. After Nicopolis (25 September 1396) Vuk's land 'was taken by the Ottomans' and 'Most of his area was transferred to the control of Stefan Lazarević' (the article places it in the 1397 context); Branković land included 'parts of Kosovo, Polimlje, Sjenica, and Brskovo'.

1402: the state becomes the Serbian Despotate. After Angora (28 July 1402) Stefan received the title of despot (August 1402) and the state 'became known as the Serbian Despotate in 1402'; the Despotate infobox gives 'Establishment: 22 February 1402', which conflicts with the Angora sequence and is not used.

1404: Sigismund grants Belgrade, Mačva and Golubac. 'Hungarian King Sigismund awarded him Belgrade, Mačva, and Golubac' (Stefan Lazarević page: 'late 1403 or early 1404'); Stefan became Sigismund's vassal and strengthened a northern border on the Sava and Danube.
1405: Belgrade becomes the capital. 'In the beginning of 1405, Stefan made Belgrade the capital of Serbia.'

region.text: Zeta, the lordship of Balša III around Skadar Lake and the coast

ledger.note: 1405: Zeta under Serbia's influence. The First Scutari War began in 1405 and Balša III 'turned to Stefan, thus bringing Zeta under Serbia's influence once again'; the page does not give the year of the turn, so 1405 is a bridge.

1411: Srebrenica to Stefan. 'Srebrnica, probably during that year, was transferred to Despot Stefan' by Sigismund; in 1415 the Bosnian parliament decided to take it back but 'it was not possible to effect' this.

region.text: Zeta, the lordship of Balša III around Skadar Lake and the coast

ledger.note: 1421: Zeta passes to Stefan. 'in 1421, before his death and under the influence of his mother, he [Balša III] passed the rule of Zeta to his uncle, Despot Stefan Lazarević'; Balša III died on 28 April 1421.

region.text: Zeta, the lordship of Balša III around Skadar Lake and the coast

ledger.note: 1421: Zeta joins the Despotate. Balša III, 'the fifth and last ruler of Zeta' (April 1403 to April 1421), bequeaths it to Stefan; Venice held Ulcinj, Bar and Budva from 1405 (Bar retaken in 1412).
July 1427: Belgrade goes back to Hungary. Stefan died on 19 July 1427 and, 'as an immediate result', Serbia returned Belgrade to the Kingdom of Hungary.
1428: Smederevo is begun as the new capital; Đurađ built it 'in 1428–1430' on the Danube.

region.text: the Despotate as in Cliopatria's 1429 shape, occupied by the Ottomans

ledger.note: 18 August 1439: Smederevo falls to the Ottomans. 'Smederevo fell on August 18, 1439'; Novo Brdo had fallen on 27 June 1441 (the occupation lasted until 1444).

region.text: the Despotate as in Cliopatria's 1429 shape

ledger.note: 15 August 1444: Serbia restored. The Peace of Szeged 'restored Serbia with borders as before 1437'; Southern Zeta stayed under Venice.

region.text: Novo Brdo, the largest mine in the Balkans

ledger.note: 1 June 1455: Novo Brdo falls to the Ottomans again. The page gives 'June 27, 1441, and again on June 1, 1455'; the Stefan Lazarević page calls Novo Brdo 'the economic center of Serbia'.

region.text: the Despotate's holdings west of the Drina (the page names no places; Srebrenica is the researcher's reading)

ledger.note: 1458: Bosnia takes the lands west of the Drina. After Lazar Branković's death (20 January 1458) 'King Stjepan Tomaš of Bosnia conquered most of the Despotate's holdings west of the Drina'.

20 June 1459: the Despotate is conquered. Infobox 'Reconquest by the Ottoman Empire: 20 June 1459'; 'Serbia was officially conquered by the Turks on June 20, 1459'; the Bosnian ruler Stephen Tomašević negotiated the withdrawal of his men from Smederevo.

wars.name: Ottoman capture of Niš
wars.outcome: Murad I took Niš from Lazar in 1386.
wars.note: The page gives the year only; the 1385 start of the war is not on it, so the span is the researcher's.

wars.name: Battle of Kosovo
wars.outcome: Tactically a draw with heavy Serbian losses; Prince Lazar and Sultan Murad I both died on 28 June 1389 (Serbian Despotate page); Serbia accepted Ottoman suzerainty in the summer of 1390.
wars.note: The Moravian Serbia page gives no day; the Despotate page gives June 28, 1389. No border change is dated in 1389.

wars.name: First Scutari War

zones.text: Zeta, the lordship of Balša III around Skadar Lake and the coast

wars.outcome: Venice seized Ulcinj, Bar and Budva in 1405; Balša III turned to Stefan Lazarević; Bar was retaken in 1412; a peace of 1408 led to 'a continuing struggle for Pomorje'.
wars.note: The Balša III page calls it 'a 10-year war, against Venice'; the Stefan Lazarević page dates the start to 1405 and the peace to 1408.

wars.name: Ottoman Interregnum
wars.outcome: Stefan Lazarević, now a despot and Hungarian vassal, stayed out of the Ottoman civil war until the Battle of Çamurlu ended it (Musa killed on the Iskar River).
wars.note: The page gives no date for Çamurlu; no border change.

wars.name: Ottoman conquest of the Serbian Despotate (1439-1444)
wars.outcome: Smederevo fell on 18 August 1439 and Novo Brdo on 27 June 1441; the Peace of Szeged of 15 August 1444 restored Serbia with its pre-1437 borders.

wars.name: Ottoman conquest of the Serbian Despotate (1455-1459)

union.text: Novo Brdo, the largest mine in the Balkans

wars.outcome: Novo Brdo fell on 1 June 1455; Bosnia took the lands west of the Drina in 1458; the Despotate was 'officially conquered by the Turks' on 20 June 1459.

certainty.note: Lazar's and Stefan's frontiers on the Morava, towards Bosnia and Zeta are approximate; the pages name towns, not lines.
The northern border on the Sava and Danube is the one firm line (Stefan Lazarević page, 1404-1427 and again from 1444); every other frontier stays soft.

notes: A split from Cliopatria's 'Serbian Empire' row (1352..1458): the Empire proper (1346-1371) is the dossier serbian-empire; this dossier is the Lazarević-Branković state that the Moravian Serbia page says 'became known as the Serbian Despotate in 1402' (one state, renamed). The orchestrator may prefer to call it serbian-despotate, but that name sits next to the Cliopatria row 'Serbian Despots' (1375..1421, 4 shapes, Montenegro/Kosovo/Albania, Wikipedia title 'Serbian Despotate') which the eu-18 part that owns serbian-despots has to settle: its 6,993 km2 shape of 1415-1421 and the end in 1421 match Balša III's Zeta (the lordship that passed to Stefan in 1421), not this state. No infobox area figure exists on any of the four pages, so the area check against Cliopatria (46,495 to 73,646 km2) is not possible. The 1415 step (+43%) is unexplained by any dated sentence (page budget). Suzerainty events are not drawn here: Ottoman suzerainty from the summer of 1390 (Moravian Serbia page), Hungarian suzerainty from 1403/1404 (Stefan became Sigismund's vassal), Ottoman vassalage again about 1447-1453 (Serbian Despotate page; the dates in that page are loose); the ottoman-empire and kingdom-of-hungary dossiers should carry the matching vassal_start and vassal_end events. Pages silent on: the Mrnjavčević land and the Altomanović land taken in 1371 and 1373 (no places), the place of Brskovo and Sjenica in the shape, Venice's control of southern Zeta after 1444 beyond a sentence, the Despotate's relation to Bar, and the Crnojević successor (Zeta under the Crnojevići is a successor in the Despotate infobox). Gazetteer names needed: Kruševac, Smederevo, Niš, Novo Brdo, Golubac, Srebrenica (places; drawn by coordinates here).
